findings.issue: Expired session documents are never deleted. Each live run that selects an ask-capable backend writes one <id>.json (up to about 96 KB) into the sessions directory. Expiry (is_expired, lines 244-248; read_session, lines 238-240) only refuses to load the file. The only cleanup, sweep_stale_tmp (lines 508-528, called from FileSessionStore::new at line 137), removes *.tmp.* files, so the directory grows without bound. Session versions 1 and 2 are also refused on read but are never removed.
findings.recommendation: Extend the sweep in FileSessionStore::new to remove <id>.json files whose created_at (or mtime) is older than the TTL, using the same cutoff logic as is_expired. Alternatively, document the retention policy and provide an explicit prune command. The sweep already runs once per live run, so the added cost is one metadata read per json file.
findings.evidence: sweep_stale_tmp filters on name.contains(TMP_MARKER) and returns before touching any non-tmp file (lines 516-518). The doc comment at lines 42-47 states the sweep covers temporary files only. A grep of crates/sc-jev-check/src for remove_file shows only tmp-file removals (lines 470, 525).

findings.issue: The session-log flush is skipped on the error path. HostRun::run calls run(self.prepared)? (line 344), so when every backend fails and run returns Err, the flush warning is never produced. The adapter is then dropped, and LoggerInner::drop discards flush and shutdown errors (crates/sc-jev-host/src/obs.rs:45-52). A flush failure on the path where failed send rows matter most is therefore silent. ask_from has the same shape: ask(...)? at compose.rs:419 returns before finish_log at line 420.
findings.recommendation: Flush before propagating the error, for example by splitting run into a match that always calls finish_log and then returns the error. When the run fails, surface the flush failure through the error's detail or the stderr channel, so the loss is observable. Keep the drop-time flush as the last resort.
findings.evidence: compose.rs:343-349 (HostRun::run) and compose.rs:418-423 (ask_from). Warning only on the success path: finish_log is reached only after the ? operator has succeeded. obs.rs:45-52 uses let _ = for both flush and shutdown in Drop.

findings.issue: The sc-observability envelope leaves request_id and correlation_id as None, while the row carries session_id and answer_id as ULIDs in fields{} only. Generic log tooling that correlates on envelope fields cannot join rows to a session or to a send.
findings.recommendation: Populate the envelope correlation field with the session id (and request_id with the answer id, if the envelope type accepts ULIDs). Keep fields{} unchanged, so the row contract does not change.
findings.evidence: ObservabilityAdapter::log_event sets request_id: None (line 196) and correlation_id: None (line 197) for every event, while event.fields() carries session_id and answer_id.

findings.issue: Every session-log event is emitted at Level::Info, whether the send succeeded or failed. A failed send (send_outcome = "failed", with error_code set) is indistinguishable by level from a successful one, so level-based filtering or alerting at WARN or ERROR cannot see failed sends.
findings.recommendation: Derive the level from the row's send_outcome: Level::Warn for failed sends and Level::Info for ok sends. Level::Warn and Level::Error both exist in sc-observability 1.5.0.
findings.evidence: log_event hard-codes level: Level::Info (line 188). The event's fields carry send_outcome, which SessionLogRow::to_fields sets to "failed" for failed sends (crates/sc-decision-schema/src/session_log/mod.rs:244-247).

findings.issue: The fixture repository is created with subprocess.run(['git','init',...], env={**os.environ, 'GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL': devnull, 'GIT_CONFIG_NOSYSTEM': '1'}). The ambient GIT_DIR, GIT_WORK_TREE, GIT_INDEX_FILE, GIT_OBJECT_DIRECTORY, GIT_COMMON_DIR and similar variables are inherited. Git hooks such as pre-commit export GIT_INDEX_FILE and sometimes GIT_DIR. When pytest is launched from such a context, 'git init' initialises or reinitialises the host repository instead of tmp_path/repo, and the later toplevel discovery from src/pkg resolves against the host. The test's CONFIG_INVALID and .env expectations then fail. Whether it fails depends on how the suite was launched, not on a random draw. The Rust side already strips these variables (crates/sc-agent-types/src/git.rs lines 98-102, and the git() helpers in crates/sc-jev-check/tests/repo.rs and crates/sc-jev-host/tests/log_context.rs), so this is the one fixture that does not.
findings.recommendation: Build the child environment from os.environ with GIT_DIR, GIT_WORK_TREE, GIT_INDEX_FILE, GIT_OBJECT_DIRECTORY, GIT_ALTERNATE_OBJECT_DIRECTORIES, GIT_COMMON_DIR, GIT_PREFIX, GIT_CONFIG_PARAMETERS, GIT_CONFIG_COUNT and GIT_DEFAULT_HASH removed. Set GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL and GIT_CONFIG_SYSTEM to os.devnull, GIT_CONFIG_NOSYSTEM=1 and GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0. Use one shared helper that mirrors the Rust git() helper, and pass a timeout (see FTQ-002).
findings.evidence: subprocess.run(["git", "init", "-q", str(repo)], check=True, env={**os.environ, "GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL": os.devnull, "GIT_CONFIG_NOSYSTEM": "1"}) followed by monkeypatch.chdir(sub) and sc_jev_py.build_request("check.toml"). The Rust production discovery strips GIT_DIR and GIT_INDEX_FILE in crates/sc-agent-types/src/git.rs:98-102.

findings.issue: subprocess.run for 'git init' has no timeout. A stalled git process, for example one blocked on a lock or a stalled filesystem, blocks the whole pytest session with no failure. Every other subprocess in the workspace is bounded by the 60 s deadline runner (tests/support/deadline.rs), so this is the one unbounded spawn in the targeted set.
findings.recommendation: Pass timeout= to subprocess.run and let subprocess.TimeoutExpired fail the test with a clear message. Better, route the call through the same bounded helper as the Rust tests, combined with the environment fix in FTQ-001.
findings.evidence: subprocess.run(["git", "init", "-q", str(repo)], check=True, env=...) with no timeout argument.

findings.issue: Two independent 20 s wall-clock budgets govern the handshake. The worker thread's deadline starts before build_request spawns the extractor. The child's own 20 s poll starts only after it has written 'started'. On a loaded host where the interpreter start is slow, the worker gives up first, never writes 'ack', and the child exits 3. The test then reports EXTRACTION_FAILED with the message 'the GIL was held', although the GIL was never the cause. The failure is intermittent on loaded CI hosts and carries the wrong diagnosis.
findings.recommendation: Remove the worker's own deadline. Let it poll for 'started' until the stop event is set, and rely on the finally block (stop.set() plus a bounded join) for the bound. Assert started.exists() before the error-code assertion, so a child that never started is reported as such. Do not widen the 20 s budgets, because that would only pad the race.
findings.evidence: answer() computes deadline = time.monotonic() + 20 before the extractor is spawned, and the handshake script (_HANDSHAKE_SCRIPT, line 363) runs its own 20 s deadline. The assertion message reads 'EXTRACTION_FAILED means the worker never ran: the GIL was held'.

findings.issue: run_from and ask_from flush the file logger through a barrier with a 5 s default timeout (sc-observability 1.5.0, DEFAULT_WRITER_SHUTDOWN_TIMEOUT and flush_with_timeout in runtime.rs). If the writer stalls past 5 s, flush returns Err. compose.rs turns that into a response warning ('session log was not flushed'). The test discards response.warnings() from both calls and then reads the JSONL file, so a flush timeout appears only as an opaque row-count assertion (rows.len() == 1 or == 2). That is intermittent under load and does not name its cause.
findings.recommendation: Assert warnings().is_empty() on the run and ask responses before reading the file, so a flush failure is named in the failure. Keep the file-level checks for paths only, and check row contents through an injected SessionLog sink, as crates/sc-jev-check/tests/session_log.rs already does. The same pattern appears outside this target at crates/sc-jev-host/tests/obs.rs lines 114 and 150 (adapter.flush().expect), and should get the same treatment.
findings.evidence: let response = run_from(source, inputs(&linked).project(label)).expect("run"); followed by let rows = rows(&linked.join(".sc-ai/logs/sc-ai.log.jsonl")); with no assertion on response.warnings(). compose.rs:428-435 converts a flush Err into a warning string. obs.rs:Drop and flush use the 5 s writer shutdown timeout.
